judge.reason: It claims an exact set of dimensions, identical to the answer in e3.

options.counterfactual: The proposed exclusion of blow-up in dimensions 3 through 18 has a substantive analytic gap, despite the successful finite-dimensional sign calculations.
options.approach: Audit the passage from an actual concentrating solution to the differentiated reduced-energy expansion. In particular, check whether cutoff forcing and parameter derivatives are controlled strongly enough to deduce boundary-jet vanishing.

options.counterfactual: A strict minimum of the proposed reduced energy does not yield the claimed sequence on one fixed smooth domain, so the dimension-19 construction is not yet established.
options.approach: Check the estimates for interactions between distinct boundary perturbations against the size of each local reduced-energy effect. The construction requires those errors to vanish relative to the local effect, not merely absolutely.

options.approach: Audit uniform invertibility and the natural-constraint argument on the fixed domain. Verify that critical points of the reduced functional solve every component of the original equation, including the bubble-kernel components.

options.counterfactual: A strict minimum of the proposed reduced energy does not yield the claimed sequence on one fixed smooth domain, so the dimension-19 construction is not yet established.
options.approach: Examine smooth compactification, positivity, and boundary concentration separately. Confirm that the constructed weak solutions extend smoothly and remain positive, and that their large values occur on the boundary.

options.counterfactual: The correct threshold is below 19 because a blow-up mechanism not captured by the polynomial boundary-shape model exists.
options.approach: Investigate whether multiple interacting bubbles can evade the positive single-bubble dilation forms in dimensions below 19. Focus on the signs and relative sizes of interaction terms in the scale equations.
